In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the development of a diagnostic test for atherosclerosis.
the synthesis of a new type of immunosorbent, i.e. a short synthetic peptide anchored to the cellulose plate.
the synthesis of short peptides mimicking the antigenic epitope from Helicobacter pyloiri urease and their use as immunogens in the diagnosis of H. pylori infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the peptides are not good mimics of the urease antigen.
the peptides are not good mimics of the antigenic epitopes of H. pylori urease.
pentapeptides are the shortest fragments of the antigenic epitope which are still able to induce the immune response in the tested sera of atherosclerotic patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the synthetic peptides are able to bind antibodies of H. pylori urease infected patients and antibodies against Jack bean urease.

a synthetic peptide with the sequence Gly-Gly-Leucine-Valine-Phenylalanine-Lysine-Threonine (GGLVFKT) mimicking the antigenic epitope on Helicobacter Pylori urease is recognized by antibodies from sera of H. pylori-infected patients and anti-JB urease antibodies.

the peptides with a Gly-Gly linker are able to bind to the anti-JB urease antibodies, and that the peptides with the triazine linker are able to recognize the antibodies from H. Pylori infected patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the peptides can be used for the preparation of a diagnostic tool for atherosclerosis.
it is possible to prepare synthetic peptides mimicking antigen of Helicobacte rpylori urease and to use them for the diagnosis of H. pylori infection.

synthetic peptides with a triazine spacer and a Gly-Gly sequence between the cellulose support and the peptide can be used for the detection of antibodies against Helicobacter urease in patients' sera.
